questions.question: Which bone is the longest and strongest of the upper limb?
questions.explanation: The humerus is identified as the longest and strongest bone of the upper limb.

questions.question: Which three main parts make up the humerus?
options: Upper end, lower end, and shaft
questions.explanation: The humerus is divided into the upper end, lower end, and the shaft connecting them.

questions.question: How many distinct features are present on the upper end of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The upper end presents five features, including the head, neck, and tubercles.

questions.question: How many distinct features are present on the lower end of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The lower end presents seven features, including the capitulum, trochlea, and epicondyles.

questions.question: In which direction is the head of the humerus directed?
questions.explanation: The head is directed medially, backwards, and upwards to articulate with the glenoid cavity.

questions.question: Which cavity does the head of the humerus articulate with?
questions.explanation: The head of the humerus articulates with the glenoid cavity of the scapula.

questions.question: Which joint is formed by the articulation of the humerus and scapula?
questions.explanation: The articulation between the humerus and scapula forms the glenohumeral or shoulder joint.

questions.question: Which part of the humerus is cylindrical in its upper half?
questions.explanation: The shaft is cylindrical in the upper half and flattened anteroposteriorly in the lower half.

questions.question: Which direction does the olecranon fossa face in the anatomical position?
questions.explanation: The olecranon fossa is located on the posterior aspect and faces posteriorly.

questions.question: Which structure covers the head of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The head is covered by articular hyaline cartilage, which is thicker in the center.

questions.question: Which neck of the humerus is a constriction at the margins of the rounded head?
questions.explanation: The anatomical neck is the constriction located directly at the margins of the rounded head.

questions.question: Which neck is the most common site for fractures due to being weaker?
questions.explanation: The surgical neck is structurally weaker and is a common site for fractures.

questions.question: Which nerve is closely related to the surgical neck of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve and circumflex humeral vessels are closely related to the surgical neck.

questions.question: Which junction is represented by the morphological neck in an adult bone?
questions.explanation: The morphological neck represents the true junction between the diaphysis and epiphysis.

questions.question: Which three muscles attach to the greater tubercle of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The greater tubercle provides attachment for the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and teres minor muscles.

questions.question: Which muscle attaches to the lesser tubercle of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The lesser tubercle provides attachment to the subscapularis muscle.

questions.question: Which muscle attaches to the floor of the intertubercular sulcus?
questions.explanation: The latissimus dorsi attaches to the floor of the intertubercular sulcus.

questions.question: Which structure is contained within the intertubercular sulcus?
questions.explanation: The intertubercular sulcus contains the long head of the biceps enclosed in a synovial sheath.

questions.question: Which muscle attaches to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus?
questions.explanation: The pectoralis major attaches to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus.

questions.question: Which border of the humerus ends in the radial fossa?
questions.explanation: The anterior border extends down and ends in the radial fossa.

questions.question: Which border of the humerus forms the medial supracondylar ridge?
questions.explanation: The lower part of the medial border is sharp and forms the medial supracondylar ridge.

questions.question: Which structure crosses the lateral border of the humerus from behind?
questions.explanation: The radial groove crosses the lateral border of the humerus about its middle.

questions.question: Which structure is located on the anterolateral surface of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The anterolateral surface presents the V-shaped deltoid tuberosity.

questions.question: Which structure is located on the anteromedial surface of the humerus?
questions.explanation: A nutrient foramen directed downwards is located on the anteromedial surface.

questions.question: Which structure lies in the radial groove on the posterior surface of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The radial groove lodges the radial nerve and profunda brachii vessels.

questions.question: Which nerve is related to the posterior surface of the medial epicondyle?
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve is related to the posterior surface of the medial epicondyle.

questions.question: Which origin is provided by the anterior surface of the medial epicondyle?
questions.explanation: The anterior surface of the medial epicondyle provides an area for the common flexor origin.

questions.question: Which muscle originates from the posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle?
questions.explanation: The posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle gives origin to the anconeus muscle.

questions.question: Which process fits into the coronoid fossa during full elbow flexion?
questions.explanation: The coronoid process of the ulna fits into the coronoid fossa during full flexion.

questions.question: Which structure fits into the olecranon fossa during full elbow extension?
questions.explanation: The olecranon process of the ulna fits into the olecranon fossa during full extension.

questions.question: Which foramen is formed when the bony bar between the coronoid and olecranon fossae is perforated?
questions.explanation: A perforation between the coronoid and olecranon fossae forms the supratrochlear foramen.

questions.question: Which ligament stretches from the supratrochlear process to the medial epicondyle?
questions.explanation: Struthers ligament is a fibrous band stretching from the supratrochlear process to the medial epicondyle.

questions.question: Which structures deviate through the supratrochlear foramen when a supratrochlear process is present?
questions.explanation: The brachial artery along with the median nerve deviates from their normal course and passes through the foramen.

questions.question: Which nerve is directly related to the surgical neck of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve is closely related to the surgical neck and can be injured in fractures.

questions.question: Which fracture commonly occurs in young individuals from a fall on an outstretched hand?
questions.explanation: A supracondylar fracture is caused by a fall on the outstretched hand and commonly occurs in young age.

questions.question: Which bony points form an equilateral triangle in a supracondylar fracture?
questions.explanation: The medial epicondyle, lateral epicondyle, and olecranon process form an equilateral triangle that remains intact.

questions.question: Which nerve is most commonly injured in a supracondylar fracture of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The median nerve is most commonly involved in the supracondylar fracture of the humerus.

questions.question: Which condition may result from injury to the brachial artery in a supracondylar fracture?
questions.explanation: Injury to the brachial artery may cause Volkmann ischemic contracture and myositis ossificans.

questions.question: Where is nonunion of a humerus fracture common due to poor blood supply?
questions.explanation: Nonunion is common if a fracture occurs at the junction of the upper and middle thirds due to poor blood supply.

questions.question: How many secondary ossification centres does the upper end of the humerus have?
questions.explanation: The upper end of the humerus has three secondary ossification centres.

questions.question: How many secondary ossification centres does the lower end of the humerus have?
questions.explanation: The lower end of the humerus has four secondary ossification centres.

questions.question: Which ossification centre may be mistaken for a fracture due to late union?
questions.explanation: The separate centre for the medial epicondyle and its late union may be mistaken for a fracture.

questions.question: Which muscle attaches to the posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle?
questions.explanation: The posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle gives origin to the anconeus muscle.

questions.question: Which nerve passes through the radial groove?
questions.explanation: The radial nerve and profunda brachii vessels are lodged in the radial groove.

questions.question: Which part of the humerus is flattened anteroposteriorly in the lower half?
questions.explanation: The shaft is cylindrical in the upper half and flattened anteroposteriorly in the lower half.

questions.question: Which structure forms the floor of the intertubercular sulcus?
questions.explanation: The latissimus dorsi attaches to the floor of the intertubercular sulcus.

questions.question: Which muscle inserts into the deltoid tuberosity?
questions.explanation: The deltoid tuberosity provides insertion to the deltoid muscle.

questions.question: Which nerve is at risk with a fracture of the surgical neck?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve wraps around the surgical neck and is at risk of injury.

questions.question: Which angle is formed by the superimposition of the long axis of the upper and lower articular surfaces?
questions.explanation: The angle of humeral torsion is formed by the superimposition of the long axis of the upper and lower articular surfaces.

questions.question: Which border of the humerus starts from the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus?
questions.explanation: The anterior border starts from the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus.
